recentMessages.text: This is a documented, already-solved problem. The composer hit exactly this: a full-screen modal inside a clamped stacking context, with the radius readout and cube drawing over its Continue button. The fix was to have the chrome stand down. The review needs the same. Checking the grid layering too.

`.review` sets `z-index: 2147483000` — a previous attempt to beat the chrome that can't work from inside a clamped stacking context, exactly as the composer comment describes. Let me confirm where my grid actually sits before fixing both.
Not my grid: those lines are inside the live slot, under an opaque review. They're the home chrome's own column dividers, which makes this one bug, not two. Reading the chrome's stand-down logic.
Now I have the established pattern. Applying it to the review: the chrome stands down, and the review reserves room for the cube exactly as the composer does.
Two more failures than before, including one new file. Checking whether that's mine.
ProfileTwin is unmodified and HEAD lacks that string, so this isn't my change. Checking whether another session just touched the test or its target.

That failure is pre-existing, not mine: it fails identically on a clean checkout of HEAD with my changes stashed. It appeared in the earlier runs too, just inside a collapsed block rather than the FAIL summary I was reading, so my "9 versus 11" comparison was measuring my own grep, not the suite. Committing.

Fixed and pushed as `a7a7135`. Sync running, phone build queued behind it.

**What was wrong.** The review screen already asked to sit on top, with a z-index of 2147483000. That can never work: it lives inside a container at z-index 4, a clamped stacking context, so nothing inside it can climb past the home chrome at 260 no matter how large the number gets. The radius card landed on "Use this" and the chrome's column rules ran down your photo.

The composer hit this exact wall before, and the comment above its own flag records the only fix that works from in there: the chrome stands down. The review now asks for the same, and reserves the same clearance so the cube keeps its seat below the buttons instead of on top of them. It gets its own flag rather than reusing the composer's, because that one also routes the cube's back gesture into the composer and this screen has Retake for that.

**Two things I checked rather than assumed.** Those vertical lines are the chrome's column dividers, not the camera grid I added today. The grid renders inside the live camera slot, underneath an opaque review, so it can't reach that screen.

And a test I briefly thought I'd broken, on the profile DM bridge, fails identically with all my work stashed. It's pre-existing. My earlier "9 failures" reading was measuring my own grep rather than the suite, so the count looked like it grew when it hadn't.

I'll report when the install lands.
install it on my phone when the build finishes
The queued task already does both; the script installs as soon as it finishes compiling. Checking where it is.

Already queued and running. The sync is mid-flight at load 20, and the build starts automatically the moment it finishes and the machine is quiet, then installs without any further input from me.

Good news on the cable: the phone now reports `wired`, so the install goes over USB rather than the Wi-Fi transport that stalled twice earlier.

Worth noting the last install did succeed over Wi-Fi at 19:47, so that transport isn't guaranteed to fail. But wired is the reliable path for a gigabyte, and that's what we have.

I'll report when it lands, with the same bundle verification I did last time.
ok its plugged in, let me know when its done
Bundle is current (20:35, after the 20:33 commit). But load has spiked to 280, and my waiter holds the build until it drops below 30. Checking what's driving it.

The build hasn't started yet, and it's not stuck; it's waiting on purpose.

**Another session is running an Android build**, at 639% CPU, which has pushed load to 280. Spotlight indexing is adding to it. My waiter holds the iPhone build until load drops under 30, and it polls every twenty seconds.

That gate is deliberate: two builds earlier today failed at load with Xcode's "too many processes" error, and a third failed on a machine that was merely busy. Starting into 280 would almost certainly waste twenty minutes and end in the same non-answer.

Everything else is ready and waiting. The bundle synced at 20:35, two minutes after the commit, so it carries the fix. Your phone is wired, so the install goes over USB.

An Android release build takes roughly half an hour from a cold start. Once it clears, the iPhone build runs about seven minutes plus the transfer, and installs on its own.

I'll tell you the moment it's on your phone.

Done. It's on your phone, installed at 20:56 over the cable once the Android build cleared and load fell to 23.

I verified the installed app rather than assuming. The capture-review event and the cube clearance are both present, and the ground paint order compiled to `function t7e(t){return FQ(t).reverse()}`, which is the widest-first ordering. The earlier batch is still aboard.

**Two things to look at.**

The camera review after a shot should now have Retake and Use this clear of the radius card, with the cube sitting below them rather than on top, and no column rules down your photo.

The map is the one I most want your eyes on. It should show each pin's territory as its own patch in that pin's colour, roughly nine of them around Toronto, sitting on the wider blue wash rather than one flat field.

**If the map is still flat**, tell me and send a screenshot rather than describing it. The remaining possibilities are opacity, which is a small change, or something in the claim source, which is a different investigation. I've been wrong twice on this one by reasoning ahead of the evidence, so I'd rather look.

**Still open from earlier:** Select and Select All in Chats wear drawn glyphs until you send icons for them. And that single account holding seven of the widest claims is worth deciding about, since it's why the wash is blue at all.

* in DM screen, these will be the icons for select and select all 
* in the feed tv, on the right rail top corner (just like the camera) we are adding side buttons:
   * block: use the block icon, this will block this user from you seeing them again and add them to your block list. create a block list in settings, where you can remove people from your block or add them
   * delete: if this is YOUR post, you can delete it straight from the feed
Two more items. Let me extract the icons and survey what block infrastructure already exists.
Icons and the block store are done; now wiring the feed's block and delete buttons, the settings block list, and the native unblock handlers, all in parallel.

Both items are done, committed and pushed. The phone install is queued behind one thing outside my control.

**Chats.** Select and Select All now wear your two icons, at every size the manifest declares, through the same registry as every other side button. The drawn stand-ins are gone.

**Feed.** The channel dial gained the same head slot the camera's filter wheel got, and two controls stand there. Block appears on someone else's post, asks first, and their pops leave the feed and map on the very next render. Delete appears only on your own post, asks first, and takes the exact native route the profile's delete uses, so the feed re-reads itself when the shell confirms.

**Settings › Blocked.** Everyone you've shut out, each with an Unblock button, plus a field to block a handle you aren't currently looking at. Unblocking puts their pops back the same way blocking removed them.

**Native handlers, both platforms.** iOS gained unblock, mirroring its existing block. Android turned out to have no block handler at all: the web posted the event, the bridge accepted it, and nothing was written, so blocks never reached the Firestore rules that close messages both ways. It now writes the same record iOS does.

There is no block icon in the set, so Block wears a drawn glyph in the card's clay, as Select did. Send one and it slots in.

The Android handlers need their own release build to reach the A03, about half an hour. I haven't started it, since it would compete with your iPhone build.

**On the install.** Another session's sync started at 21:16, twelve minutes before my commit, so the bundle it produces is stale. My job waits for it to finish, reruns the sync, then builds and installs once the machine is quiet. I'll report when it lands.
